title: 1 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 6.

questions.question: In which month did Solomon begin to build the house of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Zif
questions.explanation: Solomon began to build the house of the LORD in the month Zif, which is the second month, as stated in 1 Kings 6:1.

questions.question: How long was the house which King Solomon built for the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Threescore cubits
questions.explanation: The length of the house was threescore cubits (60 cubits) according to 1 Kings 6:2.

questions.question: What was the breadth of the porch before the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten cubits
questions.explanation: The porch before the temple was ten cubits in breadth as per 1 Kings 6:3.

questions.question: What type of windows did Solomon make for the house?
questions.correctAnswer: Windows of narrow lights
questions.explanation: Solomon made windows of narrow lights for the house, as stated in 1 Kings 6:4.

questions.question: True or False: Solomon built chambers only on the temple, not the oracle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Solomon built chambers round about against the walls of both the temple and the oracle, as shown in 1 Kings 6:5.

questions.question: What was the width of the middle chamber built against the wall?
questions.correctAnswer: Six cubits
questions.explanation: The middle chamber was six cubits broad, according to 1 Kings 6:6.

questions.question: True or False: During the building of the house, no hammer or axe or iron tool was heard inside the house.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: No hammer, axe, or tool of iron was heard inside the house while it was in building, as stated in 1 Kings 6:7.

questions.question: Where was the door for the middle chamber located?
questions.correctAnswer: Right side of the house
questions.explanation: The door for the middle chamber was in the right side of the house, as described in 1 Kings 6:8.

questions.question: What type of wood did Solomon use to cover the house?
questions.correctAnswer: Cedar
questions.explanation: Solomon covered the house with beams and boards of cedar as stated in 1 Kings 6:9.

questions.question: How high were the chambers built against all the house?
questions.correctAnswer: Five cubits
questions.explanation: The chambers built against all the house were five cubits high, according to 1 Kings 6:10.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would do if Solomon walked in His statutes and kept His commandments?
questions.correctAnswer: Perform His word with Solomon
questions.explanation: The LORD said He would perform His word with Solomon if he walked in His statutes and kept His commandments, as in 1 Kings 6:12.

questions.question: True or False: God promised to dwell among the children of Israel and not forsake them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: God promised to dwell among the children of Israel and not forsake His people Israel, as stated in 1 Kings 6:13.

questions.question: In what year of Solomon's reign was the foundation of the house of the LORD laid?
questions.correctAnswer: Fourth year
questions.explanation: The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, according to 1 Kings 6:1 and 6:37.

questions.question: True or False: The building of the house of the LORD took seven years to complete.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: It took seven years for Solomon to build the house of the LORD, as stated in 1 Kings 6:38.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 6, which of the following events happened first?
options: The word of the LORD came to Solomon
The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid
The house was covered with beams and boards of cedar
The chambers were built against all the house
questions.correctAnswer: The foundation of the house of the LORD was laid
questions.explanation: The foundation being laid in the fourth year (1 Kings 6:37) happens before the word of the LORD to Solomon (1 Kings 6:11) and before the house was covered with cedar beams (1 Kings 6:9) or chambers built (1 Kings 6:10).

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What material did Solomon use for the walls, floor, and ceiling inside the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Cedar wood and fir planks
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:15 explains Solomon built the walls within with boards of cedar and covered the floor with planks of fir, indicating the use of these woods inside the temple.

questions.question: How long did it take Solomon to build the house of the LORD from foundation to completion?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven years
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:38 states the house was finished in the eleventh year of Solomon's reign after the foundation was laid in the fourth year, making the construction period seven years.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 6:12 promise will happen if Solomon walks in God's statutes and keeps His commandments?
options: God will perform His word and dwell among Israel
Solomon will become king over all nations
The temple will never be destroyed
questions.correctAnswer: God will perform His word and dwell among Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 13 together promise that if Solomon obeys God's laws, God will fulfill His promise to David and dwell among the children of Israel, showing the blessing of obedience.

questions.question: How were the cherubims inside the oracle described in terms of size?
options: Each was ten cubits high with wings spanning ten cubits
Each was five cubits high with wings spanning twenty cubits
Each was twenty cubits high with wings spanning ten cubits
Each was ten cubits high with wings spanning five cubits
questions.correctAnswer: Each was ten cubits high with wings spanning ten cubits
questions.explanation: Verses 23 and 24 specify that each cherub was ten cubits high and their wings stretched five cubits each, totaling ten cubits from wingtip to wingtip.

questions.question: What does the covering of the temple's interior with gold teach us about honoring God in worship?
options: That we should offer our best and most precious to God
That gold is necessary for all worship
That wealth is a sign of God's favor
That outward beauty is more important than inner holiness
questions.correctAnswer: That we should offer our best and most precious to God
questions.explanation: Verses 20-22 describe the temple and altar overlaid with pure gold, illustrating giving God the highest honor and offering our best in worship and service.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 6:19, what was placed in the oracle within the temple?
options: The ark of the covenant of the LORD
The tablets of the Ten Commandments
questions.correctAnswer: The ark of the covenant of the LORD
questions.explanation: Verse 19 specifically states the oracle was prepared to set the ark of the covenant there, highlighting the centrality of God's presence in the temple.

questions.question: How does the passage in 1 Kings 6:14-16 demonstrate the importance of careful preparation in serving God?
options: Solomon built the house with detailed woodwork and precise dimensions
Solomon hurried the construction to finish quickly
Solomon built the temple only with stone and no wood
Solomon left the interior unfinished for later
questions.correctAnswer: Solomon built the house with detailed woodwork and precise dimensions
questions.explanation: Verses 14-16 show Solomon finished the house with cedar boards on walls and floors, and precise measurements for the oracle, demonstrating dedication and diligence in God's service.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Kings 6:18, no stone was seen inside the house because all the interior was covered with carved cedar.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states the cedar inside was carved with knops and open flowers and that no stone was seen, indicating the entire interior was wood-covered for beauty and sanctity.

questions.question: What virtue can believers learn from the fact that Solomon built the temple with no iron tools heard during construction (1 Kings 6:7)?
options: Respect for holiness and careful work
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for holiness and careful work
questions.explanation: Verse 7 reveals that no iron tools were heard during building, symbolizing reverence in constructing God's house, teaching believers to approach sacred work with respect and carefulness.

questions.question: How does the construction of the temple's inner court with hewed stone and cedar beams (1 Kings 6:36) teach about balance in Christian life?
options: That wood is superior to stone
questions.correctAnswer: Balance between strength (stone) and growth/flexibility (wood)
questions.explanation: Verse 36 describes three rows of hewed stone and one row of cedar beams, symbolizing the need for both strength and spiritual growth or flexibility in Christian living.

questions.question: What does the carving of cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers on the walls and doors teach about worship in 1 Kings 6:29-32?
options: Worship involves creativity and beauty honoring God
Only plain walls are acceptable in worship
Gold is more important than carvings
questions.correctAnswer: Worship involves creativity and beauty honoring God
questions.explanation: Verses 29-32 detail carved figures and gold overlay, showing that artistic beauty and creativity are ways to honor God in worship and sacred spaces.

questions.question: True or False: The oracle's dimensions were twenty cubits in length, breadth, and height as described in 1 Kings 6:20.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 20 clearly states the oracle's measurements were twenty cubits in length, breadth, and height, emphasizing its perfect cubic shape as a holy space.

questions.question: What is the significance of Solomon making a golden partition by chains before the oracle (1 Kings 6:21) for believers today?
options: It illustrates the separation of the holy from the common and reverence for God's presence
It shows that gold is necessary for worship
It means the temple was locked
It shows that chains symbolize bondage
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the separation of the holy from the common and reverence for God's presence
questions.explanation: Verse 21 mentions a gold partition by chains before the oracle, teaching believers the importance of reverence and recognizing God's holiness by setting apart sacred space.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Kings 6:14, Solomon only started building the house but did not finish it.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 14 explicitly states that Solomon built and finished the house, showing completion and faithfulness in God's work.

questions.question: How does the detailed description of the cherubims' wings touching the walls and each other (1 Kings 6:27-28) teach about unity in the body of Christ?
options: The cherubims’ wings touching symbolize close unity and harmony
The cherubims were isolated from each other
questions.correctAnswer: The cherubims’ wings touching symbolize close unity and harmony
questions.explanation: Verses 27-28 describe the cherubims with wings touching walls and each other, teaching believers about the importance of unity and harmony within God's household.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 6.

questions.question: How were the wings of the cherubims arranged within the inner house of Solomon's temple?
options: The wings touched each other in the middle and each wing touched a wall
The wings were folded against their bodies
The wings touched only the floor
questions.correctAnswer: The wings touched each other in the middle and each wing touched a wall
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:27 describes that the wings of the cherubims stretched so that one wing touched one wall, the other wing touched the opposite wall, and their wings touched one another in the midst of the house.

questions.question: What material did Solomon use to overlay the cherubims inside the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Gold
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 6:28, Solomon overlaid the cherubims with gold, showing the preciousness and sanctity of the temple decorations.

questions.question: Besides cherubims, what other figures were carved on the walls inside and outside the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Palm trees and open flowers
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:29 states that carvings of cherubims, palm trees, and open flowers adorned the walls both within and without the temple.

questions.question: True or False: The entire floor of the temple was overlaid with gold, both inside and outside.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:30 confirms that the floor of the house was overlaid with gold within and without, emphasizing the temple's grandeur.

questions.question: From which type of wood were the doors of the oracle made?
questions.correctAnswer: Olive tree
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:31 specifies that the doors for entering the oracle were made of olive tree, with significant decorative carvings and gold overlay.

questions.question: What proportion of the wall did the lintel and side posts of the oracle doors constitute?
questions.correctAnswer: One-fifth
questions.explanation: The lintel and side posts of the oracle doors were a fifth part of the wall as stated in 1 Kings 6:31.

questions.question: How were the two doors of the temple itself constructed and decorated?
options: Made of cedar with iron hinges
Made of fir tree with folding leaves, carved and overlaid with gold
Made of olive tree with no carving
questions.correctAnswer: Made of fir tree with folding leaves, carved and overlaid with gold
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:34-35 describe the temple doors as made of fir tree with folding leaves, carved with cherubims, palm trees, and flowers, and covered with gold fitted upon the carved work.

questions.question: What was the structure of the inner court surrounding the temple?
options: Two rows of hewed stone and a row of cedar beams
Three rows of hewed stone and a row of cedar beams
Four rows of hewed stone and no beams
One row of hewed stone and three rows of cedar beams
questions.correctAnswer: Three rows of hewed stone and a row of cedar beams
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 6:36, Solomon built the inner court with three rows of hewed stone and a row of cedar beams, combining stone and timber construction.

questions.question: How many years did Solomon spend building the temple, and in which months did the foundation and completion occur?
options: 5 years; foundation in Nisan, completion in Tishri
7 years; foundation in Zif, completion in Bul
10 years; foundation in Adar, completion in Kislev
3 years; foundation in Iyar, completion in Shevat
questions.correctAnswer: 7 years; foundation in Zif, completion in Bul
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:37-38 records that the foundation was laid in the month Zif (second month) in Solomon's fourth year, and the house was finished in the month Bul (eighth month) in the eleventh year, totaling seven years.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage closely relates to the cherubim imagery found in Solomon’s temple, especially regarding their protective and symbolic role?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 25:18-22
questions.explanation: Exodus 25:18-22 describes God’s instructions for making two cherubim of gold over the mercy seat of the Ark of the Covenant, echoing the cherubim Solomon placed inside the temple (1 Kings 6:23-28), symbolizing God's presence and protection.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Hebrew word 'cherubim' (כְּרוּבִים) used in this chapter, especially regarding their role in the temple?
options: Guardians or attendants of the divine presence
questions.correctAnswer: Guardians or attendants of the divine presence
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'cherubim' (כְּרוּבִים) traditionally refers to angelic beings who serve as guardians of God's holiness and throne, fitting the temple context where they symbolize God's presence (1 Kings 6:23-27).

questions.question: In terms of literary structure, what device is evident in the description of the cherubim’s wings touching the walls and each other in the middle of the temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The description in 1 Kings 6:27 where the wings touch the walls and then each other in the center forms an inclusio framing the inner sanctum, highlighting the sacred space’s completeness and unity.

questions.question: True or False: The oracle within Solomon’s temple was a cube measuring twenty cubits on each side and was overlaid with pure gold.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:20 describes the oracle as twenty cubits in length, breadth, and height, overlaid with pure gold, emphasizing its perfection and holiness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God dwelling among His people as promised in 1 Kings 6:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Revelation 21:3
questions.explanation: Revelation 21:3 states, 'Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them,' echoing the promise of God's dwelling among Israel in 1 Kings 6:13.

questions.question: What theme in 1 Kings 6:12-13 about obedience and God's presence fulfills an earlier covenant promise made to David?
options: The assurance of God's perpetual dwelling with Israel if they obey
The mandate to build many altars
questions.correctAnswer: The assurance of God's perpetual dwelling with Israel if they obey
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:12-13 reiterates God's promise to David that if Solomon obeys His statutes, God will dwell among Israel and not forsake them, fulfilling the Davidic covenant found in 2 Samuel 7.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What specific divine promise does God give Solomon concerning the temple if Solomon obeys God's statutes, judgments, and commandments?
options: God will grant Solomon long life
God will dwell among the children of Israel and not forsake His people
God will multiply Solomon’s wealth and honor
God will make Solomon’s name famous among all nations
questions.correctAnswer: God will dwell among the children of Israel and not forsake His people
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:12-13 shows that God promises to dwell among Israel and not forsake them if Solomon walks in His statutes and keeps His commandments, emphasizing God's covenant faithfulness and presence.

questions.question: What theological significance does the absence of iron tools heard in the temple's construction reveal about the sanctity of the house?
options: It symbolizes purity and holiness in the temple's construction
It indicates a lack of available resources
It demonstrates the builders' fear of noise
It shows the temple was built hastily
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes purity and holiness in the temple's construction
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:7 states that no hammer, axe or iron tool was heard in the temple as it was built, symbolizing the sanctity and purity of God's house, reflecting the holiness required for God's dwelling place (cf. Exodus 20:25).

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 6:2, what were the dimensions of the temple Solomon built, and what might these dimensions represent theologically?
options: Length 60 cubits, breadth 20 cubits, height 30 cubits; representing God’s perfect order and majesty
Length 100 cubits, breadth 50 cubits, height 40 cubits; symbolizing God's overwhelming power
Length 30 cubits, breadth 10 cubits, height 15 cubits; indicating humility before God
Length 70 cubits, breadth 30 cubits, height 25 cubits; pointing to Israel’s military strength
questions.correctAnswer: Length 60 cubits, breadth 20 cubits, height 30 cubits; representing God’s perfect order and majesty
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:2 details the temple’s exact measurements, which reflect divine order and majesty, consistent with biblical themes of God's perfect and holy habitation (cf. Ezekiel 40:5).

questions.question: What doctrine about God's covenant faithfulness is illustrated by the phrase 'which I spake unto David thy father' in 1 Kings 6:12?
options: The doctrine of the Davidic Covenant as an unconditional promise
The doctrine of covenant renewal contingent on obedience
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of covenant renewal contingent on obedience
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:12 shows God’s promise to Solomon to fulfill the word spoken to David, highlighting covenant continuity that is conditional on obedience, consistent with biblical covenant theology (cf. 2 Samuel 7).

questions.question: How does the detailed description of the cherubim in 1 Kings 6:23-27 reflect the theological understanding of God's presence?
options: Cherubim symbolize God’s holiness and serve as guardians of His throne
Cherubim are mere decorations with no theological significance
Cherubim indicate the temple’s architectural complexity
questions.correctAnswer: Cherubim symbolize God’s holiness and serve as guardians of His throne
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:23-27 describes two large cherubim overlaid with gold in the inner sanctuary, symbolizing God’s holy presence and His throne, consistent with their role in Exodus 25:18-22 and Ezekiel 10.

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by His promise to 'not forsake my people Israel' in 1 Kings 6:13?
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: The promise in 1 Kings 6:13 reveals God's faithfulness to His covenant people, assuring His continual presence and commitment despite human actions.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching emerges from the description of the temple’s inner walls covered with cedar and gold (1 Kings 6:15-16) and the cherubim carved on the walls (1 Kings 6:29)?
options: The holiness and beauty of God's dwelling place reflects His glory and the need for reverence
The temple was primarily a royal palace rather than a holy place
The use of cedar and gold shows Israel’s wealth was more important than worship
The carvings indicate idolatry was permitted in the temple
questions.correctAnswer: The holiness and beauty of God's dwelling place reflects His glory and the need for reverence
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:15-16 and 29 together depict the temple’s splendor with precious wood, gold, and sacred imagery, teaching that God’s dwelling is holy and glorious, demanding reverence (cf. Psalm 96:6).

questions.question: What theological significance does the seven-year construction period of the temple (1 Kings 6:37-38) have in the redemptive narrative?
options: It symbolizes completeness and divine perfection in God's plan
It indicates human inefficiency in worship preparation
It reflects the passing of a generation
It shows the temple was a minor project
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes completeness and divine perfection in God's plan
questions.explanation: The seven years mentioned in 1 Kings 6:37-38 echo biblical symbolism of completeness (cf. Genesis 2:2), indicating God's perfect timing in establishing His dwelling for redemption history.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 6:20-22’s emphasis on overlaying the temple and altar with pure gold contribute to our understanding of the divine attribute of holiness?
options: Gold symbolizes purity and the transcendent holiness of God's presence
Gold was a symbol of wealth and power only
Gold was used to impress foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: Gold symbolizes purity and the transcendent holiness of God's presence
questions.explanation: The extensive use of pure gold in the temple and altar in 1 Kings 6:20-22 symbolizes the purity and holiness of God’s presence, underscoring His transcendence and glory (cf. Exodus 28:36-38).

questions.question: Sceptics claim the elaborate temple construction was merely a political show of power. What does 1 Kings 6:11-13 actually teach about the purpose of the temple?
options: The temple's purpose was to provide a physical place for God's presence if Israel obeyed His laws
The temple was built solely for Solomon's glory
The temple was a fortress for defense
The temple was a secular administrative building
questions.correctAnswer: The temple's purpose was to provide a physical place for God's presence if Israel obeyed His laws
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:11-13 records God's word to Solomon that the temple was to be a dwelling place for God among Israel contingent upon obedience, emphasizing its spiritual purpose over political display.

questions.question: What does the construction of winding stairs to chambers within the temple (1 Kings 6:8) symbolize in terms of sanctification and approach to God?
options: The gradual progression and ascent towards holiness and God's presence
A secret path for priests to escape
questions.correctAnswer: The gradual progression and ascent towards holiness and God's presence
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:8 describes winding stairs ascending through temple chambers, which can be theologically interpreted as symbolizing the spiritual ascent and sanctification process required to approach God (cf. Hebrews 7:19-22).

questions.question: What doctrine is underscored by Solomon finishing the temple exactly according to the pattern and measurements given (1 Kings 6:14, 38)?
options: The doctrine of divine order and covenant faithfulness in worship
The doctrine of human innovation in worship
The doctrine of improvisation in religious practices
The doctrine of mere external appearances
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine order and covenant faithfulness in worship
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:14 and 38 emphasize Solomon’s faithful adherence to the divine pattern, teaching the importance of divine order and covenant faithfulness in worship (cf. Exodus 25:9).

questions.question: What theological insight arises from combining the temple’s gold overlay (1 Kings 6:21-22) and the carved images of cherubim and palm trees (1 Kings 6:29-32)?
options: God’s holiness is both glorious and intimately present through symbolic artistry
The temple was a place of idolatry
The temple emphasized human craftsmanship over divine presence
The temple’s decoration was purely ornamental without meaning
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness is both glorious and intimately present through symbolic artistry
questions.explanation: The combination of pure gold overlay and sacred carvings in 1 Kings 6:21-22 and 29-32 signifies that God’s holiness is both transcendent and immanently present, communicated through rich symbolism (cf. Exodus 25:18-22).

questions.question: How does the description of chambers and their varying widths around the temple walls in 1 Kings 6:5-6 relate to the doctrine of God's provision and order in worship?
options: They demonstrate God’s orderly provision for priests and temple functions
They show arbitrary architectural choices without theological meaning
They indicate the temple was a residential palace
questions.correctAnswer: They demonstrate God’s orderly provision for priests and temple functions
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:5-6 explains chambers built around the temple with specific measurements, indicating God’s ordered provision for worship and priestly duties, underscoring divine orderliness (cf. Leviticus 16).

questions.question: What narrative arc in redemptive history does the building of Solomon’s temple in the fourth year of his reign (1 Kings 6:1) signify?
options: The transition from wilderness tabernacle worship to a permanent temple of God
The renewal of the Mosaic law
questions.correctAnswer: The transition from wilderness tabernacle worship to a permanent temple of God
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 6:1 marks the beginning of temple construction, signifying the movement from the nomadic tabernacle to a permanent temple, a major step in God's redemptive plan for His people (cf. Exodus 25–40).
